html:
The Bantustans, or homelands, were territories set aside under apartheid for black South Africans by ethnic group, created under a law of 1959 to make the black majority citizens of separate states rather than of South Africa.

Built on the reserves of the Natives Land Act, they covered about 13 percent of the land. From 1976 four, Transkei, Bophuthatswana, Venda and Ciskei, were declared independent, though no other country recognised them. Millions of people were forcibly moved into them.

They were poor, overcrowded and dependent on wages sent home by migrant workers. Their leaders were often corrupt and kept in power by Pretoria. All were reabsorbed into South Africa at the election of 1994, when apartheid ended.
sum: The Bantustans, or homelands, were territories set aside under apartheid for black South Africans by ethnic group, created under a law of 1959 to make the black majority citizens of separate states rather than of South Africa.
